task: Round 10, narrow target: the word-order assertion binder in .agent-harness/scripts/check_ssot_consistency.py at HEAD 32ba566, and nothing else. Commit 915e2e4 DELETED the distance-ranking binder that round 9 broke (F-COMMA-ADJACENCY) and replaced it with bind_by_word_order(): the clause is walked in order, each run of consecutive ids forms one subject group, the group takes the FIRST status token that follows it, and that token is consumed and never offered to a later id. A group with no following token falls back to the token immediately before it. Genuine ambiguity is reported as 'unresolved' only when a competing EARLIER token is dangling, meaning no group claimed it. Separately, coverage was made asymmetric: contradictions are still detected at the full ASSERTION_WINDOW however phrased, but only an AFFIRMATIVE connector from a closed allowlist may add an id to 'covered'. This is brand-new load-bearing code that has never been adversarially reviewed, and it decides whether a false statement about a gate is caught. Break it. Questions to answer EXECUTABLY by mutating a scratch copy and running the checker, recording exact exit codes and exact output, never by reading and reasoning alone: can any ordinary-looking sentence still bind a gate id to a status that is not its own, in either direction? what happens with three or more ids and two or more tokens interleaved, with ids inside parentheses or quotes, with an id appearing twice on one line, with a status token appearing twice, at the ASSERTION_WINDOW boundary and one character either side of it? can the BOUNDARY_RE clause splitter be used to sever a lie from its detection, or to fuse two clauses that should be separate? the board-row path find_board_assertions runs BEFORE the prose path and its results are marked affirmative by construction -- can a table row be crafted so the two paths disagree, or so the board path grants coverage the prose path would refuse? can the dangling-token rule be inverted, i.e. can an attacker make a real conflict look non-dangling by adding a decoy id, or make an innocent line look dangling to force a false error? can the affirmative allowlist be satisfied by text a human would read as a denial, or can a legitimate affirmative form be excluded so the coverage floor fails on honest prose? does _negated interact correctly with the new binding, and can negation be used to suppress a contradiction rather than merely to withhold coverage? Report the attacks that FAILED too, with their exact inputs -- an attack surface reported clean without saying what was tried is not evidence.
